target.title: fix(auth): use sanitized profile name for Codex import even without id- prefix
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where openai codex oauth import profile name collision (pr #100844).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
If `accountId` is missing, the function only accepts `profileName` if it starts with `"id-"` (which is the case for subject-based names, not email-based names). If `profileName` is an email (e.g. `user@example.com`), it does not start with `"id-"`, so the function falls back to a static `fallback` string (e.g. `"hermes-import"`). When migrating multiple credentials, they will all share the same fallback profile name, causing migrations to collide or overwrite each other.

Affected location: `[src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.ts](file://src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.ts#L132-L138) (compiled as `dist/provider-auth-3I4RpGfo.js`)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Sanitize and return the profile name (such as emails) even if it doesn't start with `"id-"`:
  ```javascript
  function resolveOpenAICodexImportProfileName(identity, fallback) {
      if (identity.accountId) return `account-${identity.accountId.replaceAll(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+/gu, "-")}`;
      if (identity.profileName) return identity.profileName.replaceAll(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+/gu, "-");
      return fallback;
  }
  ```

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: When migrating OpenAI Codex profiles (e.g. from Hermes), stable identity details like the profile email should be used to construct a unique, sanitized profile name if `accountId` is not present, avoiding name collisions.

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Reproduction / regression tests in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.test.ts` run and pass successfully.

### Real Behavior Proof

#### Unique Import Name Resolution Verification:
We executed a verification script passing email-based profileName strings. The outputs show that they successfully resolve to distinct sanitized values instead of colliding on the fallback name:

```text
[VERIFICATION] Import Profile Resolution:
  Identity 1 (peter@example.com) resolved name:    peter-example.com
  Identity 2 (john.doe@example.com) resolved name:  john.doe-example.com

[SUCCESS] Profile names are uniquely resolved and sanitized, avoiding name collision!
```
